items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bill Perkins played tenor and Chico played drums.

ctx.x: Dick Bock, that’s right. I was gonna say… yeah, Dick Bock, B-O-C-K, yeah. He was a good guy. And… Chico recorded for him. And then Dick put together this record that… it’s called Two Degrees East, Three Degrees West, which is, was an ironic title

because I was supposed to be one of the Three Degrees West. Bill Perkins played tenor and Chico played drums. And I was from Cleveland, so I wasn’t from the West Coast at all (laughs) and… and John Lewis was from Texas, I think, and Percy, he… Anyway, it was, it was great. It was Percy and John, and that’s where I kinda got to know John, who was an incredible help to me after that so…
Before we get to New York and John, you also came across Brookmeyer and Jim Giuffre and (this was?)…
